Theme

Household, washing & chores · Nature & food

stake noun

a post or prop for plants

also prop, post, pole (for plants), vine prop, bean pole, support (for a plant)

classical

Plaut. Mil. 4.4.4: ut fīgam pālum in parietem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.5.11 (Lewis & Short)

pālus, pālī m.

noun, second declension

a stake, a post, a prop

Other words

  • ridica, ridicae f. — a vine prop, a stake

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 17 (Lewis & Short); Varr. RR 1.8.4 (Lewis & Short); Col. 4.26.1 (Lewis & Short)

    The farm writers’ word.

  • adminiculum, adminiculī n. — a prop, a support for a vine

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. ND 2.120: vītēs clāviculīs adminicula, tamquam manibus apprehendunt (Lewis & Short)

    At first the vine-dresser’s word for the pole a vine climbs; then any support (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • hic docuit teneram pālīs adjungere vītem

    he taught men to tie the tender vine to stakesTib. 1.7.33

  • vītēs clāviculīs adminicula, tamquam manibus apprehendunt

    vines take hold of their props with their tendrils as if with handsCic. ND 2.120 (Lewis & Short)

See also tie, vine, tendril, fence, rod.

SourcesLewis & Short: palus · Lewis & Short: ridica · Lewis & Short: adminiculum

Tibullus, Elegiae 1.7.33.
